title: Arrays, shapes, and vectorized metrics
relevance: Embedding batches and latency metrics use array operations. A wrong axis gives plausible but incorrect quality reports.

sections.title: Shape describes your contract
paragraphs: A NumPy ndarray stores typed values in a multidimensional shape. A matrix shaped (runs, tests) has one row per run. sum(axis=0) reduces the run axis and produces one value per test. sum(axis=1) produces one value per run.
Vectorized operations apply across arrays efficiently. A boolean mask selects observations. Slices can share memory with the original array, so use .copy() when mutation should be isolated.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
passed = np.array([[1, 0, 1], [1, 1, 0]])
print(passed.shape)  # (2, 3)
print(passed.mean(axis=0))  # rate for each test

sections.title: Broadcasting rules
paragraphs: NumPy compares trailing dimensions. Dimensions match when equal or when one is 1. An array of shape (3,) can be added to (2, 3); an array of shape (2,) cannot without reshaping to (2, 1).

The result may be valid mathematically but wrong semantically. Label axes before operations. Explicitly choose floating-point dtype before division or normalization; integer storage can truncate derived values.
sections.code:
latency = np.array([[100., 200., 300.], [120., 220., 330.]])
baseline = np.array([100., 200., 300.])
print(latency / baseline)

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: For a duration table shaped [builds, tests], axis=0 aggregates across builds and axis=1 aggregates across tests. Keep axis names in comments or variable names because an array does not retain the meaning of its coordinates automatically. A scalar, row vector and column vector have different broadcasting behavior.

Boolean masks select elements satisfying a condition; using a mask with the wrong shape can fail or select the wrong subset. Check dtype and finite values before computing statistics. Integer arrays are appropriate for IDs but floating-point arrays are needed for normalized metrics. Test a one-row table, a one-column table, empty arrays and NaN values. Compare vectorized output with a small explicit loop as an independent oracle.

mistake: Broadcasting a baseline along the wrong axis silently compares unrelated observations.
takeaway: Write the meaning of each axis alongside its shape.

title: Cosine similarity from first principles
objectives: Compute dot product and vector norms
relevance: Semantically similar failures may have different text. Vector similarity is a useful candidate signal, but it is not proof of the same root cause.

sections.title: A vector is a representation
paragraphs: A vector is an ordered list of numeric coordinates. An embedding model learns representations whose geometry can capture useful relationships. The synthetic vectors in this lab are hand-designed for arithmetic practice; they are not real semantic embeddings.

The dot product sums pairwise coordinate products. A norm measures length. Cosine similarity divides the dot product by both lengths, so it compares direction. Cosine 1 means the same direction; 0 is orthogonal; -1 is opposite.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([1., 2., 0.])
b = np.array([2., 4., 0.])
print(np.dot(a, b))  # 10
print(np.linalg.norm(a))  # sqrt(5)

sections.title: Normalization and distance
paragraphs: A unit vector is v / norm(v). For unit vectors the dot product equals cosine similarity. Squared Euclidean distance between unit vectors is 2 - 2*cosine, so they induce the same ranking. Unnormalized dot product also rewards magnitude.
A zero vector has no direction, so cosine is undefined. Reject it or apply a documented fallback. Do not divide by zero and hope NaN sorting will produce sensible retrieval results.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: Raw dot product rewards magnitude as well as direction. For a=[1,0], b=[10,1] and c=[1,0], b has a larger dot product than c but lower cosine similarity. This difference matters when an index is configured for dot distance while embeddings are not normalized.

A zero vector has no direction. The teaching implementation returns a declared zero score, while another application may reject it; either policy must be explicit and tested. Reject mismatched dimensions rather than letting zip silently truncate coordinates. In retrieval, keep document identity aligned with vector rows, and test identical, opposite, orthogonal and zero vectors. Geometric similarity remains evidence for ranking, not proof that two failure causes are the same.

mistake: Vectors from different models or dimensions are not comparable, even if their text looks related.
takeaway: Similarity is a geometric candidate signal that still needs domain validation.

title: Sampling, masks, and reproducible experiments
objectives: Separate deterministic fixtures from statistical samples
relevance: Reproducible synthetic CI history helps compare analyzer versions without depending on proprietary data.

sections.title: Random does not mean uncontrolled
paragraphs: Use np.random.default_rng(seed) and keep the seed with the experiment. A fixed seed helps reproduce one sample but does not prove stability across samples. Sample multiple seeds when estimating uncertainty.
A mask such as durations > 5 identifies slow observations; np.percentile returns a tail summary. The mean can hide a small group of severe outliers, so retain raw observations and relevant segments.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
durations = rng.lognormal(mean=1, sigma=0.5, size=100)
print(np.percentile(durations, 95))
print(durations[durations > 5].size)

sections.title: Representative samples
paragraphs: Sampling only successful production interactions creates survivorship bias. Include unsuccessful requests, rare categories, long inputs, empty retrieval, and adversarial inputs in separately labeled slices.
Keep training, tuning, and final evaluation samples separate. Changing a prompt repeatedly against the final evaluation set effectively trains your decisions on that set.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: A random seed reproduces a pseudo-random sequence under a fixed implementation and data order; it does not make a sample representative. Uniform row sampling can underrepresent rare product defects or repeat many rows from one incident. Stratification preserves selected class proportions, while group sampling avoids splitting closely related incidents across partitions.

Report which sampling unit was used: run, test, incident or build. For uncertainty estimates over correlated runs, resample independent incidents rather than individual repeated observations. Keep a sealed holdout that was not inspected during iteration. Test that sampled IDs are valid, groups are disjoint where required and every necessary class has coverage. Reproducibility and representativeness are separate evaluation properties.

mistake: A fixed seed gives repeatability, not a guarantee that the sample represents production.
takeaway: Version both the sampling method and the resulting evaluation dataset.

exercise.prompt: Your evaluation set contains only successful chatbot interactions. What is the main issue?
exercise.explanation: Filtering for success removes precisely the failures you need to understand.

title: Matrix shapes and normalized batch similarity
objectives: Matrix shapes and normalized batch similarity
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects matrix shapes and normalized batch similarity with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Vectorized scoring is useful for transparent exact-retrieval reference results.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Embedding search can score many documents at once with a matrix product. If queries have shape [q,d] and documents [n,d], normalize each row and multiply queries by documents transposed to obtain [q,n]. Each output row is one query's score against every document.

The shared dimension d is a contract, not a value that can be reshaped arbitrarily. A transpose changes axes; reshape reorganizes the same flat storage. Confusing them can return the right dimensions with the wrong numerical relationships.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Compute row norms with axis=1 and keepdims=True, then divide using a zero-safe output. This broadcasts one norm per row across its d coordinates. Matrix multiplication @ performs a dot product along the shared dimension; elementwise * does not aggregate.

For queries [[1,0],[0,1]] and documents [[1,0],[1,1]], normalized scores are [[1,.707],[0,.707]]. Test against the manual cosine calculation before trusting a large batch. Keep dtype and finite-value checks at the boundary.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
q=np.array([[1.,0.],[0.,1.]])
d=np.array([[1.,0.],[1.,1.]])
d=d/np.linalg.norm(d,axis=1,keepdims=True)
print(q@d.T)

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Normalizing the whole matrix by one global norm changes ranking assumptions. Dividing integer arrays in place can fail or truncate under an inappropriate dtype. An empty document collection requires a correctly shaped empty score matrix, not an index error.
Check dimension mismatch, zero rows, non-finite values and each result's query/document identity. Use small hand-computed matrices as an independent oracle.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Vectorized scoring is useful for transparent exact-retrieval reference results. Measure its runtime separately from embedding generation and compare numerical results with the single-vector implementation.

For SDETs, shapes and mathematical invariants are powerful tests: normalized nonzero rows have norm one, self-similarity is one and orthogonal similarity is zero. They can detect wrong axes without requiring a large model or provider account.

mistake: Normalizing the whole matrix by one global norm changes ranking assumptions. Dividing integer arrays in place can fail or truncate under an inappropriate dtype. An empty document collection requires a correctly shaped empty score matrix, not an index error.
takeaway: Vectorized scoring is useful for transparent exact-retrieval reference results.
